news.h: Pansar bags RM170.9m subcontract for water infrastructure upgrade in Sarawak
news.body: Pansar Bhd has secured a letter of acceptance (LOA) from KKB Engineering Bhd for a RM170.9m subcontract involving the second phase of water infrastructure upgrades in Samalaju, Sarawak. Pansar said its wholly-owned subsidiary Perbena Emas Sdn Bhd had accepted the LOA for civil and structural works of the project, which is part of the Sarawak Corridor of Renewable Energy (SCORE). Work includes the construction and completion of buildings and infrastructure for a raw water intake facility with a capacity of 160.0m litres per day (MLD), pumping mains, a 120 MLD water treatment plant and associated facilities. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Pansar's wholly owned Perbena Emas has accepted a RM170.9m letter of acceptance from KKB Engineering.
The job is civil and structural works for the second phase of water infrastructure upgrades in Samalaju, Sarawak, part of SCORE.
Scope includes a 160 MLD raw water intake facility, pumping mains and a 120 MLD water treatment plant.
This board's 2 October digest recorded KKB Engineering winning a RM517m Sarawak water-infrastructure contract. Today's item does not say whether Pansar's subcontract sits under it.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Pansar or KKB Engineering. Digest context only.

news.h: SSF Home buys 13-acre industrial land in Pulau Indah for RM42.5m
news.body: SSF Home Group Bhd is acquiring three parcels of leasehold industrial land in Pulau Indah, Mukim Klang, Selangor, for RM42.5m to build its own warehouse and distribution facilities, according to a press statement issued on Monday (Oct 26). The transaction is being executed via its wholly-owned subsidiary, SSF Sdn Bhd, which entered into a conditional sale and purchase agreement with IFFCO Foods Sdn Bhd. The three vacant parcels of land cover a combined area of approximately 52,611.13 sq m, or 13 acres, and are designated for industrial use. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: SSF Home is buying three vacant leasehold industrial parcels in Pulau Indah, Selangor, for RM42.5m.
The land will be used for its own warehouse and distribution facilities.
The buyer is its wholly owned SSF Sdn Bhd, under a conditional SPA with IFFCO Foods Sdn Bhd.
The parcels total about 52,611 sq m (13 acres), roughly RM808 per sq m (computed here). The digest gives no funding source or completion date.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of SSF Home. Digest context only.

news.h: Econpile bags RM24.4m piling job for 53-storey KL apartment project
news.body: Econpile Holdings Bhd has secured a RM24.4m contract to undertake site clearing, retaining wall and piling works for a 53-storey serviced apartment project along Jalan Tun Razak, Kuala Lumpur. The contract was awarded to its wholly owned subsidiary Econpile (M) Sdn Bhd by REIN Architects Sdn Bhd, on behalf of Beverly 37 Sdn Bhd. The proposed development comprises 315 serviced apartment units, seven levels of podium parking, two basement parking levels and other facilities. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Econpile has won a RM24.4m contract for site clearing, retaining wall and piling works.
The project is a 53-storey serviced apartment development on Jalan Tun Razak, Kuala Lumpur.
The award went to Econpile (M) Sdn Bhd from REIN Architects, on behalf of Beverly 37 Sdn Bhd.
The development comprises 315 units, seven podium parking levels and two basement levels. The digest gives no contract period.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Econpile. Digest context only.

news.h: West River bags RM17.9m in M&E jobs for Puchong, Bukit Jalil residential projects
news.body: West River Bhd through its wholly owned subsidiary West River Engineering Sdn Bhd (WRE) has secured two mechanical and electrical (M&E) subcontracts worth a combined RM17.9m in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur. West River Engineering won an RM11.0m contract for a proposed apartment development in Puchong, Selangor, and a RM6.9m air-conditioning and mechanical ventilation (ACMV) contract for Park Green serviced apartments at Pavilion Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: West River Engineering has won two M&E subcontracts worth a combined RM17.9m.
RM11.0m is for an apartment development in Puchong, Selangor.
RM6.9m is an ACMV contract for Park Green serviced apartments at Pavilion Bukit Jalil. The two sum to RM17.9m (reconciles).
This board's 6 October digest recorded a separate RM17.5m West River subcontract for a Selangor logistics park.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of West River. Today's Kenanga ESG Update on M&E contractors does not include it. Digest context only.

news.h: Aneka Jaringan secures RM53.4m piling contract for IOI Properties project
news.body: Foundation and basement construction specialist Aneka Jaringan Holdings Bhd has secured a RM53.4m contract to undertake piling works for the proposed Rio City Town Centre development in Selangor. Rio City Town Centre is part of IOI Properties Group Bhd's 100-acre IOI Rio City integrated development in Bandar Puteri Puchong. The development has an estimated gross development value of RM12.0b and will comprise residential, office, retail and hospitality components, including the planned IOI Mall Rio. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Aneka Jaringan has won a RM53.4m piling contract for the proposed Rio City Town Centre in Selangor.
Rio City Town Centre is part of IOI Properties' 100-acre IOI Rio City development in Bandar Puteri Puchong.
The development has an estimated GDV of RM12.0b, with residential, office, retail and hospitality components, including the planned IOI Mall Rio.
This is revenue for the contractor, not IOIPG. The digest's top-loser table shows IOIPG closing at RM3.18 (-0.6%) on 26 October.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Aneka Jaringan. IOIPG last appeared as a row in this board's 28 August Results Note (MARKET PERFORM, RM4.09). Digest context only.

macro.h: EU plans to hit China with more import curbs in early 2027 — Bloomberg
macro.body: The European Union is planning to use safeguard measures to cut imports of products from sectors including chemicals, furniture and machinery from China, according to people familiar with the matter. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The EU plans safeguard measures to cut imports from China, according to people familiar with the matter.
Sectors named include chemicals, furniture and machinery.
The headline dates the curbs to early 2027 and credits the report to Bloomberg.
The digest gives no tariff rates or quota sizes.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: Rural road programme expenditure of RM6.108b over 2023-2025 within revised allocation — Zahid
macro.body: Expenditure under the Rural Roads Programme (JALB) for the 2023-2025 period totalled RM6.108 billion, within the revised allocation of RM6.143 billion, leaving a balance of about RM34.3 million, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Spending under the Rural Roads Programme (JALB) totalled RM6.108b over 2023-2025.
That is within the revised allocation of RM6.143b.
The stated balance is about RM34.3m. The rounded figures give about RM35m (computed here), so the difference is presumably rounding (an inference).
The figures come from Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: Net disposable income approach to aid eligibility assessment from 2027 — deputy minister
macro.body: The government will implement the net disposable income (NDI) approach in 2027 to ensure that the assessment of eligibility for aid takes into account demographic factors and liabilities, in addition to income. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The government will use a net disposable income (NDI) approach to assess aid eligibility from 2027.
The assessment will consider demographic factors and liabilities, not only income.
The source is a deputy minister, per the headline.
The digest does not say which aid programmes are affected.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: Loke: RM1,000 driver aid to be disbursed nationwide, not just in Melaka
macro.body: Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook has denied that the RM1,000 special financial assistance given to taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Melaka on Monday was intended to fish for votes ahead of the Melaka state election. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Melaka received RM1,000 of special financial assistance on Monday, 26 October.
Transport Minister Loke Siew Fook denied the payment was meant to win votes ahead of the Melaka state election.
The headline says the aid will be disbursed nationwide.
The digest gives no total cost or nationwide timetable.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.body: The USD50 billion (RM204 billion) investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang. (The Edge Malaysia)

takeaways: Thailand's imports grew at their fastest pace on record in September.
The drivers cited are higher energy costs and an investment boom in AI and advanced electronics.
Demand rose for fuel and capital goods.
The digest gives no growth figure.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: US, Canada working on deal to ease steel, auto tariffs, sources say
macro.body: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, two US and four Canadian sources said, as the two governments try to repair relations that soured after trade talks broke down in August. (Reuters)
takeaways: The US and Canada are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and autos.
The report rests on two US and four Canadian sources.
Relations soured after trade talks broke down in August.

reports.name: ESG Update: Mechanical & Electrical — Winning Orders Is Only Half the Battle
reports.conviction: "KEEMING (OP; TP: RM2.84) remains our sector top pick."
reports.flag: Six points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The Kenanga Signal rests on Kenanga's own words. Pages 1 and 4 both read 'KEEMING (OP; TP: RM2.84) remains our sector top pick', which is a pick declaration under rules/signals.md §2 and is quoted on the row. 'Remains' implies an earlier pick. This board's own 4 September KEEMING Results Note carried no pick language, so this is the first time the board records the pick. The document is headed 'ESG Update' on page 1 and 'Sector Update' on pages 2-6. It is filed as a Sector Update because the report-type dropdown is fixed to five types (rules/signals.md §6), the same treatment as the 13, 19 and 21 October ESG Thematic rows. (2) HEGROUP's turnover is stated two ways, by two methods. Page 3 gives a calculated 29.0%, then 31% two paragraphs later. Page 1's methodology divides FY25 departures by FY25 year-end headcount. Page 3 says it divides them by the average of the FY24 and FY25 headcounts. The note does not reconcile these. A footnote also says HEGROUP's 8.5 training hours per employee uses 1,114 hours, and its separate 1,063-hour table would give 8.1. (3) Some ratios are rounded generously. The 'up to 2.5-fold' gap in revenue per employee, RM0.6m to RM1.6m, is about 2.7x on the printed figures. The same applies to 'SUNLOGY generating 2.5x higher revenue per employee' than CHEEDING. The '14-fold' order-book gap, RM0.4m to RM5.2m, is 13x (all computed here). The unrounded inputs are not given. (4) The peer table is the wider utilities table. It is headed 'UTILITIES', and its Sector Aggregate market cap of RM175,927.5m is identical to the aggregate in today's YTLPOWR note, which also lists TENAGA, PETGAS, YTLPOWR, MALAKOFF and GASMSIA. The eight stocks shown here total RM10,149.5m (computed here). The aggregate growth, PER and yield figures therefore appear to describe the wider universe, not these eight (an inference). Of the seven contractors compared, only KEEMING and CHEEDING are in the table. CBHB, MNHLDG, JATI, SUNLOGY and HEGROUP carry no Kenanga rating in this note. (5) Peer-table ratings and targets against this board. KEEMING RM2.84 matches the 4 September row, CHEEDING RM0.78 the 28 August row, SOLARVEST RM3.76 the 23 September mention, and SAMAIDEN RM3.20 the 8 October strategy note. SWIFT is shown as OUTPERFORM at RM0.47, against MARKET PERFORM at RM0.40 in this board's 28 August SWIFT Company Update and the 22 October WPRTS peer table. The 21 and 28 September rows flagged the same discrepancy. It is not reconciled here, and no SWIFT figure is used. Three OUTPERFORMs sit outside Kenanga's own bands, approximating expected total return as upside + net dividend yield (an inference, not a Kenanga method statement): PEKAT (-25.5% upside), SOLARVEST (-11.1%) and SAMAIDEN (6.7% + 1.0%). Upsides reconcile with the printed prices and targets. The table gives no price date. (6) Charts are images. Exhibit 1's headcounts cannot be reliably matched to companies from the extracted text, so only JATI's 136 employees, which the text states, is used. Typographical slips are carried as printed: 'a up to 2.5-fold' and 'or simply reflective of'. This row has no rating, target or share price, so those columns are empty by design.
reports.catalyst: Kenanga's ESG team compares seven listed M&E contractors (KEEMING, CHEEDING, CBHB, MNHLDG, JATI, SUNLOGY, HEGROUP) on workforce. It finds an up to 2.5-fold gap in revenue per employee (RM0.6m-RM1.6m) and a 14-fold gap in order book per employee, but neither a lean workforce nor a big order book reliably delivers better margins. Project mix, pricing and subcontractor management matter as much. It calls staff turnover, and thin disclosure of it, an underappreciated execution risk. The sector stays OVERWEIGHT, and KEEMING (OP; TP RM2.84) remains its sector top pick.
reports.quote: We maintain our OVERWEIGHT call on the M&E sector, supported by sustained data centre and electrical infrastructure investments.
summary: The frame and the call. Kenanga says data centre and electrical infrastructure investment is enlarging M&E contractors' order books, so delivering projects profitably, and with enough skilled staff, is becoming as important as winning them. It compares seven listed players using FY25 annual reports, except KEEMING and CHEEDING (FY26). Per-employee metrics use year-end direct headcount, excluding subcontracted manpower. The sector stays OVERWEIGHT, and KEEMING (OP; TP RM2.84) remains its sector top pick, 'riding on multiple growth opportunities in data centres and solar'.

Productivity is not margin. Revenue per employee ranges from RM0.6m (CHEEDING) to RM1.6m (KEEMING). SUNLOGY also generates about RM1.6m but has the lowest GP margin, 11%, so only RM0.2m of GP per employee. CBHB generates RM1.5m and the highest GP per employee, RM0.5m, on a 34% margin. CHEEDING has the lowest revenue productivity but the highest GP margin, 56%, for RM0.35m of GP per employee. Because subcontracted workers are excluded from headcounts, outsourcing-heavy contractors can look more productive than they are. Kenanga says inconsistent disclosure prevents a meaningful quantitative comparison.

Workforce mix and retention. Only three companies disclose a comparable mix: KEEMING 81% permanent (FY26), CBHB 54% and JATI 45% (FY25). On turnover, HEGROUP is a calculated 29.0% (see flag), against company-reported rates of 18.9% for KEEMING, 16.6% for SUNLOGY and 14.4% for CHEEDING. MNHLDG leads training intensity at 16.7 hours per employee, with CBHB and HEGROUP at about 8.5 and KEEMING at 2.6. Identified training spend is RM107,871 at CBHB, RM70,706 at CHEEDING and RM16,682 at KEEMING. Kenanga concludes that training hours alone do not explain retention.

Order books against headcount. Order book per employee ranges from RM0.4m (HEGROUP) to RM5.2m (JATI). JATI carries RM710m of outstanding orders with 136 employees, 3.6x its FY25 revenue, the highest cover. CBHB follows at RM4.0m per employee (2.7x) and MNHLDG at RM2.2m (2.1x). Bigger books do not mean better margins: JATI's FY25 GP margin was 14%, CBHB's 34%, and CHEEDING's 56% on only RM0.9m per employee. Kenanga says a high order book per employee does not automatically mean manpower strain, because subcontractors add capacity and contracts are recognised over different timelines.

Earnings implications. Under IFRS S1, Kenanga traces workforce risk to earnings through three channels: delays from skilled-labour shortages, higher recruitment, training and subcontracting costs, and productivity and margin pressure. It says the impact must be assessed company by company, not assumed for the sector. Limited disclosure on departures of skilled staff makes the earnings effect hard to size, so Kenanga calls it an underappreciated execution risk and asks for more transparency on retention, training and subcontractor reliance. In the peer table, KEEMING (RM2.48) offers 14.5% upside and CHEEDING (RM0.540) 44.4%, both OUTPERFORM.

analyst.note: Checked for KEEMING, the stock this note names as its sector top pick. The most recent dated call from a named non-Kenanga house read in full during this run is Maybank Investment Bank, as reported by The Edge Malaysia under the dateline 18 August. The article prints no year. It is read as 2026 because it says the shares had risen more than six times since a February listing, to RM2.40 (an inference). That is 70 days before this note. Maybank 'downgraded Kee Ming to ‘hold’ from ‘buy’ on valuation', with no target price stated and no pick language. The Analyst Signal therefore reads None stated. reports.name: YTL Power International Berhad
reports.flag: Six points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) 'We continue to like YTLPOWR' is not a pick declaration. The investment case reads 'We continue to like YTLPOWR for: (i) its earnings stability... and, (ii) its longer-term growth potential'. This board has treated the same wording as investment-case language, not a Top Pick, sector pick or most-attractive call (GAMUDA, 22 September-15 October; ANCOMNY, 19 October). No other conviction-search term appears, so the Kenanga Signal reads None stated. (2) The share-price claim does not match the close. Kenanga says its full-year scenario, a 4.9% cut to FY27 net profit, 'broadly reflects the share price decline since last Friday's close' 'at time of writing'. Today's digest shows YTLPOWR closing 26 October at RM4.96, down only 0.8%, and the note's own RM4.96 price implies about RM5.00 on Friday (computed here). The intraday low may have been deeper. This run did not establish that, and the claim is reported as written. The note's KLCI figure, 1,611.28, matches the 23 October close, not 26 October's 1,604.4. (3) The 18-day sensitivity rounds up. Scaling the full-year 4.9% to 18 days gives about 0.24% (computed here); the note prints 0.3%. Both are immaterial, as Kenanga says. (4) Market cap and share count differ across pages. The cover gives RM44,903.5m on 8,787.4m shares, which implies about RM5.11 a share, not RM4.96 (computed here). The peer table's RM43,585.4m is consistent with RM4.96 on 8,787.4m shares. The sum-of-parts uses 8,724m issued shares: RM55,852m divided by 8,724m gives RM6.40 (reconciles). The SoP components also sum to RM6.40. (5) Table oddities. The ratio table prints 'ROA' twice. The second row (18.8% / 12.3% / 7.7% / 9.4% / 10.2%) does not match the DuPont ROE row (20.7% / 12.7% / 7.8% / 9.9% / 10.6%), so its label is unclear. The capex row is blank. FY27F operating cash flow of RM15,725m, against RM2,117m in FY26, is not explained in this note. In the peer table, PETGAS is MARKET PERFORM at about 13.1% (8.9% upside + 4.2% yield), above the 10% line, and PEKAT and SOLARVEST are OUTPERFORM with negative upside. This is the same approximation as on earlier rows, an inference rather than a Kenanga method statement. SWIFT appears at OP, RM0.47, the same unreconciled discrepancy flagged on today's M&E row. (6) Market data. The 52-week range of RM2.51-6.02 is from stockanalysis.com, not Kenanga, and matches the note's cover. The 1.57% dividend yield is stockanalysis.com's figure at its RM5.10 close on 27 October, a day after the note's price. Kenanga's own FY27F net yield is 1.6% (8.0 sen).
reports.catalyst: Indonesia cut piped gas to Singapore from 24 October: 31 MMSCFD for 18 days, under 2% of Singapore's daily gas demand. YTLPOWR's shares came into focus. Kenanga calls the hit financially immaterial. PowerSeraya's operations have not been disrupted, because sole buyer GasCo is reallocating supply, including extra LNG. A 1.0% squeeze on PowerSeraya's PBT margin would cut FY27 net profit by 0.3% over 18 days, or 4.9% over a full year. Forecasts, the RM6.40 SoP target and OUTPERFORM are maintained, and Kenanga calls any share-price weakness a buying opportunity.
reports.quote: We maintain our earnings forecasts, TP of RM6.40 and OUTPERFORM rating, viewing any share price weakness as a buying opportunity.
summary: The call. Kenanga keeps its forecasts, its sum-of-parts target of RM6.40 and OUTPERFORM. At RM4.96 the target implies 29.0% upside (peer table; also computed here). The target matches the RM6.40 recorded in this board's 3 September Market Strategy row. FY27F/FY28F core net profit stays at RM2,190m/RM2,514m, about 6% and 8% below consensus of RM2,335m/RM2,746m (computed here). Core EPS is 25.1/28.8 sen and core PER 19.8x/17.2x. No ESG adjustment is made to the target (three-star rating).

The event. According to SKK Migas, Indonesia's upstream regulator, gas exports to Singapore were cut from Saturday, 24 October, to divert more gas to domestic power generation. The cut is 31 MMSCFD: 15 from Natuna and 16 from Sumatra. Singapore's Energy Market Authority says this is under 2% of the country's daily gas demand and will last 18 days. Singapore's Minister for Manpower and Second Minister for Trade and Industry said short-term electricity prices are unlikely to be affected.

Why the effect is small. In May 2025 the EMA created Singapore GasCo to centralise gas procurement for power generation, which is about 95% of national electricity supply. GenCos' existing contracts are grandfathered. PowerSeraya has run without disruption since Saturday, which Kenanga credits to GasCo's ability to draw extra LNG at the SLNG Terminal and reallocate supply across plants. Management says Indonesian piped gas is 30% of PowerSeraya's gas needs. If the cut lasts longer than 18 days, Kenanga says GasCo can buy more seaborne LNG.

The sensitivity. Kenanga sees the main risk as slightly higher costs for replacement gas, and expects the impact to be mild because costs are blended across the sector. A 1.0% compression in PowerSeraya's PBT margin over 18 days would cut YTLPOWR's FY27 net profit by 0.3%. Over a full year, its conservative scenario, it would cut it by 4.9%. Kenanga says the share-price fall since Friday broadly prices in the full-year case (see flag).

Valuation, investment case and risks. The RM6.40 SoP comprises Singapore IPP RM1.53, Wessex RM1.53, the data centre business RM2.94 (a 10% discount to RM79m EV per MW on 1,158MW by FY30), YES RM0.23, Ranhill RM0.22, the new IPP RM0.16 and other investments RM0.29, less RM0.50 of net debt. Kenanga cites earnings stability from regulated assets worldwide and longer-term growth from data centres and digital banking. The risks it names are stringent ESG standards in developed markets, Singapore power-sector regulation, the data centre business failing to take off, sustained losses at YES, and AI diffusion rules. FY27F NDPS is 8.0 sen, a 1.6% yield.

On divergence: no verified call rates YTLPOWR opposite to Kenanga's OUTPERFORM, so the marker is not set. crossCheck.note: The cut's size matches independent reporting. The Jakarta Post (24 October) reports, citing SKK Migas chief Djoko Siswanto, a 31 MMscfd reduction: 15 MMscfd from Natuna and 16 MMscfd from Sumatra, made 'to maintain the reliability of domestic gas supply for electricity'. It reports Singapore's EMA as saying the cut is under 2% of total daily gas demand. That article gives no end date; it says SKK Migas will monitor the situation daily. The 18-day duration rests on Kenanga's attribution to the EMA and was not confirmed in this source. Today's digest shows YTLPOWR as the most-traded KLCI stock on 26 October (43.22m shares), closing at RM4.96 (-0.8%), with YTL Corp down 5.3%.
